summary: This bill reauthorizes and modifies the Conrad State 30 program, which allows foreign doctors to obtain waivers from a two-year home residency requirement if they practice in underserved areas, by extending the program, adjusting waiver allotments, and clarifying employment protections and eligibility requirements for participating physicians.

scores.thoughts: This bill is entirely focused on immigration policy related to foreign physicians. It extends and modifies the Conrad State 30 program, which allows foreign doctors to waive a two-year home residency requirement if they practice in underserved areas in the U.S. The bill also makes changes to physician national interest waivers and other immigration procedures for doctors. The overall effect is to make it easier for foreign physicians to remain and work in the U.S., particularly in underserved areas, which increases immigration of a specific professional group.
